description: Whether the metric is deterministic given pinned artifacts, windows, tool versions, and parameters.
Whether contract-side logic remains constant-time or otherwise tightly bounded.
Whether on-chain state can stay compact as histories grow.
Whether updates can be made per release or batched window rather than high-frequency events.
Whether inputs are hash-anchored artifacts or signed attestations rather than unverifiable services.
Whether third parties can recompute and compare the metric from public committed evidence.
Whether metric evidence is bound to a stable developer identity and provenance path.
Whether archive hashes, version identifiers, and evidence records prevent artifact substitution.
Whether the metric can be encoded as bounded integers or fixed-point values.
Whether the metric resists low-cost manipulation in a public-ledger context.
